My post will be a little different than most.

I'll preface with honesty: I haven't been following this sport as closely as I have in the past. Since the WC, I've watched Liverpool play less than 15 times. I am a Liverpool fan and normally catch at least 30 games live a season.

I remember my first few times watching Raheem play. I was so impressed by his work rate and his willingness to defend. The way that kid used his body was absolutely unbelievable for his size, shape and age. He was very strong and boxed out incredibly well. I suppose his personality in life didn't match his play style.

But I wish the kid all the best.

He is a talent and Liverpool fans should support one of their most promising International players. You guys often look for reasons to hate people. You have one here. Change your ways if you want to see success for England. I can't stress enough how toxic your football culture is for players.

Raheem was playing very well up until after the christmas break last season. He became a shadow of himself after that, probably with all the contract talk and so on in the background it might have worn him down. He has the potential to be a great, hopefully the media won't be on his back ( what am I talking about, the english media love building up players only to break them down) and he can go on to flourish for both club and country.

That's a shame, but most players are not good enough, or lucky enough to have an entire career of success and good play.

I wouldn't devalue him too much based on a poor season. Especially considering the things I've read about his struggle to feel comfortable. I do think athletes are comfort creatures to the extreme degree

What he needs now, as you've said, is for people to lay off him and support his talent.

I know a lot of English football fans through the internet. They seem to desire international success above all else. You know what gets you that? Making your players comfortable. Unfortunately, 9/10 modern footballers will need to be coddled to reach their potential. I understand your culture as a whole is against coddling, but you have to sacrifice to get what you want. Support your players. English media will lay off when the average fan stops reacting well to negative stories.

I believe, not only for this reason, that it's on you guys to push your team forward. Encourage wild play. Your youth players will grow up with youtube. They will watch Ronaldinho videos. Messi videos. Encourage this. Don't make your players afraid of making mistakes. Help them dare to try new things.

That's just my 2 cents.

City are paying a premium here.

  • QPR's share of the profit

  • English

  • Young, talented (first team ready), and load of potential.

  • Unwilling seller

Add those factors up and you get a hefty transfer fee.

I should preface by saying I think Sterling is overrated. But I get why people like him.

I guess it's just the deal in the context of other deals. I look at Raheem Sterling getting 50m for Liverpool and think shit, Lacazette would be a damned steal under 30m. Bale at 85m is a fuckin bargain. Herrera at 29, Isco at 23. All suddenly look absolutely amazing.

You could have bought Griezmann and Isco and had a couple million left over. Or Cuadrado and Schurrle. Or Lallana and Benatia. Or Oscar and Lavezzi.

Or Raheem Sterling.

So with Toure and Silva guaranteed starters. Fernandinho seems pretty locked in. Nasri seems set too. I can see Sterling slotting in above Navas, but then I put it in perspective and think that it makes this deal that much worse. City just paid 50m for a Navas replacement who's not a particularly inspiring winger without a particularly inspiring cross. Which would be ok.

Except 50m.

And that's assuming they go 4-5-1 and don't start Dzeko, which might be pushing it. Cause if they do, who sits? Nasri? I guess. But you paid 50m for a Nasri replacement? Seems a poor choice when the defense has been so questionable at times.

I don't get it.

I am a neutral, so I am playing devil's advocate. IMO, it is an expensive transfer, but I can see why City did this.

City are old, and in need of an overhaul. Their future signings will need to cover a few variables;

  • Young - They cant keep signing old players, they need younger players to replace their aging first team. Other than Mangala their defense is old as fuck and should be priority over other positions.

  • Home Grown - They are very low on home grown talent, and need more first team talent. Hart and Clichy are the other two regular starters who are home grown. They are desperate. They lost Milner + Lampard + Richards.

  • Experienced Talent - City is not in a position to be patient and to groom undeveloped talent, they need players experience to fill first team roles.

Sterling is all 3. He is the only person available who fits all three criteria and City would have been stupid not to overpay in this specific set of circumstances.

But wait......That is not all.

QPR get a share of the profit. So it is not as if Liverpool gets the entire 50m, and Liverpool drove the price up to a point they felt comfortable selling because they knew they would get what they felt was a fair price, which may end up being around 35m after all is said and done.

Yes City could have gone out and bought all sorts of players, but none of them are home grown (apart from Bale and Lallana). City need to begin trimming the roster of unused talent, and will need to spend big on young, experienced, home grown talent and expect more of this type of spending in the future. Why do you think City is linked to Wilshere every year?
